column1: # Every package a nook part can install, one per line, so ./nook can offer each one on its own.
# Columns (tab separated): id · parts · on · what it is for · fedora · debian · arch · suse
#   parts  which parts want it: plasma, tile.<part> (tile.hypr, tile.shell …), shell.<tool>
#          (shell.zoxide …: one switch per tool in ./nook → shell), several with commas
#   on     1 = picked by default when its part is picked, 0 = offered but off
#   names  the distro's package name(s), space separated; - = not there (install by hand);
#          @name = done by nook itself (@vt323 is downloaded, @quickshell built on Ubuntu,
#          @lazygit from COPR atim/lazygit, @opencode from npm or its installer)
# Hyprland comes from COPR sdegler/hyprland (Fedora) or PPA cppiber/hyprland (Ubuntu); the
# installer enables those only when a package from them is picked.
